react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this metabolomics study. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052, FDR = 7.52e-15, fold enrichment 1453) as rank 2, while the same pathway in the KEGG human-specific namespace (hsa00052) achieved rank 1 in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 5.65e-09). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked galactose metabolism at position 4 (p = 0.0068) with a 12/13 compound overlap, the highest overlap ratio in its output. The five driver metabolites are galactitol (KEGG:C01697), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and sucrose (KEGG:C00089). Galactitol is the reduced form of galactose and a diagnostic marker of galactosemia; galactinol is the galactosyl donor substrate for myo-inositol glycosylation; sucrose provides an exogenous hexose source feeding the Leloir pathway; myo-inositol is a phosphatidylinositol precursor linking membrane lipid signaling to this sugar metabolism cluster. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed five distinct first-block identifiers across the driver metabolites with zero structural conflicts. Pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid, detomidine, phenylacetic acid, D-glucose, and methimazole did not map to the galactose cluster, suggesting peripheral involvement or off-target effects. MetaboAnalystR detected a secondary signal in phenylalanine metabolism (hsa00360, p = 0.0298), but this is a single-metabolite hit of lower statistical weight. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies a coherent carbohydrate/glycosylation shift centred on galactose utilization.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on the same primary signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 7.52×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment ≈1500×) placed Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052) as the top-two hits, with five input metabolites — galactitol, galactinol, glycerol, myo-inositol, sucrose — matching the pathway roster. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this metabolomics study. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052, FDR = 7.52e-15, fold enrichment 1453) as rank 2, while the same pathway in the KEGG human-specific namespace (hsa00052) achieved rank 1 in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 5.65e-09). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked galactose metabolism at position 4 (p = 0.0068) with a 12/13 compound overlap, the highest overlap ratio in its output. The five driver metabolites are galactitol (KEGG:C01697), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and sucrose (KEGG:C00089). Galactitol is the reduced form of galactose and a diagnostic marker of galactosemia; galactinol is the galactosyl donor substrate for myo-inositol glycosylation; sucrose provides an exogenous hexose source feeding the Leloir pathway; myo-inositol is a phosphatidylinositol precursor linking membrane lipid signaling to this sugar metabolism cluster. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed five distinct first-block identifiers across the driver metabolites with zero structural conflicts. Pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid, detomidine, phenylacetic acid, D-glucose, and methimazole did not map to the galactose cluster, suggesting peripheral involvement or off-target effects. MetaboAnalystR detected a secondary signal in phenylalanine metabolism (hsa00360, p = 0.0298), but this is a single-metabolite hit of lower statistical weight. The cross-paradigm consensus identifies a coherent carbohydrate/glycosylation shift centred on galactose utilization.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
